## Easter Island after your main tour: when it is an optional extension

[Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), lies far from mainland Chile. Visitors discover the culture of the moai, ceremonial platforms, volcanoes, and the Pacific coastline. For a journey through several South American countries, reaching the island requires a separate flight and a dedicated section of the itinerary.

A genuine extension is available with the [14-day tour through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/). Its main route passes through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), Cusco and Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni, and Atacama, and finishes in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). **Easter Island is offered separately as a 3-day, 2-night extension**, so adding it increases the overall length of the trip.

However, a tour appearing among optional destinations does not necessarily mean the island is an add-on: other active itineraries already include days on Rapa Nui as part of the journey. Before comparing options, open each tour and check its actual daily itinerary, included excursions, and route flights.

## When the island is an extension and when it is already on the itinerary

| Format | What matters |
|---|---|
| [14 days through the Andes](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) | The island is a separate extension |
| [12 days: Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/) | Days on the island are already described |
| [3 days on Rapa Nui](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) | A standalone short trip |

In the [12-day itinerary through Argentina, Patagonia, and Santiago](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/), the island appears in the tour title and in the daily descriptions, with visits to [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), and other sites. The question here is what the already advertised island portion includes, rather than automatically adding another 3 days to the trip.

Travelers who want a journey devoted entirely to Rapa Nui culture can choose a [standalone three-day itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). It offers a useful comparison with an island extension to a longer trip. Easter Island is also part of the main daily sequence in the [17-day private grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/).

## What to include in three additional days

Rapa Nui's key sites are closely tied to the islanders' history and ceremonial traditions. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is known for the places where moai were carved; Ahu Tongariki has restored statues standing on a stone platform; Orongo is associated with the birdman ceremony; and Anakena combines a beach with archaeological remains.

The optional program attached to the [Peru, Bolivia, and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) includes Rano Raraku, Tongariki, Anakena, Orongo, and Ahu Akivi. The precise order and actual selection of visits should nevertheless be checked against the approved island program: listing several places does not override national park restrictions.

Rapa Nui National Park is managed by the local Ma'u Henua community. Visitors need a separate entrance ticket and an accredited accompanying guide to access its sites; entry to some sensitive areas is restricted. This is an important part of planning, especially when only a few days remain after a busy mainland journey.

## Flights, documents, and time allowances

The island extension is generally reached via Santiago, a convenient finishing point for a mainland itinerary. Flying to Rapa Nui requires dedicated travel time and checks of available flights, baggage allowances, and possible connections. Plan for the calendar days spent flying both ways, not just the nights on the island.

Rapa Nui has its own special entry regime. Chilean government rules require the relevant form, proof of accommodation at an accredited property, and a return ticket. Entry documents for Chile itself depend on nationality and route; those requirements must be checked separately for the travel dates and should not be confused with permission to stay on the island.

The extension to the [14-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) specifies 3 days and 2 nights on the island. These days do not replace the mainland portion: the additional program lengthens the entire trip and requires coordination of flights and accommodation. The guiding language, entrance fees, and excursion conditions should also be confirmed.

## Who should choose an island extension?

If your main interest is Rapa Nui culture and its archaeological sites, extra days on the island let you experience something absent from the continental route through the Andes. Travelers with limited vacation time may instead prefer a tour that already includes the island and has its itinerary arranged in advance.

Compare [tours in Chile](/chile/tour/) and the [standalone Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) by number of nights, flights, and sites visited. The phrase "can be added" applies only to an explicitly confirmed optional component of a particular tour; it should not conceal mandatory island days in other programs.

## Frequently asked questions about extending a trip to Easter Island

### Are three days enough for Rapa Nui?

The active 14-day mainland itinerary offers an extension of 3 days and 2 nights. With an agreed schedule, this allows an introduction to major sites, but it is not the same as exploring the entire island in depth.

### Is Easter Island included in the basic 14 days of the Andes tour?

No. On the [tour through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), it is a separate three-day program.

### Do I need a guide to visit the moai?

An accredited guide is required when visiting Rapa Nui National Park. Check entrance tickets and the rules for individual archaeological sites before your trip.

### Can I visit without additional flights?

No. Adding the island to a mainland tour involves an air journey and time for connections. Check its cost and whether it is included in your selected fare.

## Easter Island tours: three days among the moai or a longer journey through Chile

[Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), sits in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. Its main attractions are stone moai statues, ceremonial ahu platforms, volcanic craters, and traces of the islanders' culture. You can choose a short trip devoted entirely to the island or an itinerary that combines several days on Rapa Nui with South American cities and natural regions.

The overall duration of a tour is only a starting point. Part of a six-day trip is spent in Santiago and on flights, while on a 17- or 33-day journey the island is just one stop. What matters more is **the number of actual sightseeing days on Rapa Nui**, the sites covered, and the arrangements for traveling between the mainland and the island.

## Rapa Nui's main sites: why travelers choose these routes

Most cultural itineraries focus on several archaeological areas. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is a volcano whose slopes were used to carve many of the moai; figures in different stages of completion can still be seen here. [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is famous for its platform with 15 restored statues. These two sites are often combined on a journey along the southern coast.

A different story unfolds around [Rano Kau volcano](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) and the ceremonial [village of Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/). This area is associated with the birdman tradition and the special status of the island's clans. [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) reveal other aspects of monumental architecture and stoneworking.

[Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) adds the ocean and white sand to the archaeological visits. Several itineraries include it as a stop after seeing the moai. Whether swimming is possible depends on the conditions that day. Rapa Nui National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its archaeological monuments are protected heritage, not unrestricted places to wander.

## Short itinerary: Easter Island in 3 days

The [Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) lasts **3 days and 2 nights**. On the first day, after meeting at the airport, travelers visit Rano Kau and Orongo. The second day follows the southern coast through Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki to Anakena. Day three covers Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau, and Tahai, followed by an airport transfer.

This option lets you focus on the island without a long mainland itinerary. It includes private excursions with an English-speaking guide, accommodation at a 4-star hotel, and transfers as specified in the program. You should check how your chosen flights fit the beginning of the first excursion and the end of the last. The visiting days are already set; additional nights or a different order of sites are not included automatically.

## Santiago and Rapa Nui: 6 or 10 days

[Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) is a **6-day** itinerary. After exploring the Chilean capital and coast, travelers fly to the island. Visits on Rapa Nui include Orongo, Rano Raraku, Tongariki, Anakena, Ahu Akivi, and Puna Pau. The city and island portions are more compact than those on longer journeys.

The [10-day private tour of Chile and Easter Island](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) gives you more time to explore the country. First come Santiago, Valparaíso, and Viña del Mar, followed by several days on the island: separate excursions cover Anakena and archaeological zones, Orongo and Rano Kau, and Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau. For travelers seeking a more detailed program without crossing into other countries, that is a significant difference from the six-day option.

## Easter Island together with Atacama and Patagonia

[Best of Chile in 12 Days with Easter Island](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) combines the island with Santiago, the Atacama Desert, and the mainland's high-altitude landscapes. Several days near the end of the journey are devoted to Rapa Nui. Actual transfer times are particularly important here: two 12-day itineraries can allocate time among moai, mountains, and cities very differently.

The [12-day Argentina, Patagonia, Santiago, and Rapa Nui itinerary](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/) adds Buenos Aires and the natural regions of the southern continent. This is a multi-country journey involving separate flights, rather than an extended vacation spent entirely on the island.

For a longer trip, there is a [17-day private grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) visiting Rapa Nui, Atacama, Patagonia, and Iguazú. Its island days include Rano Kau, Orongo, Ahu Tongariki, Anakena, and Ahu Akivi. A private charter flight to the island is provided on this trip, setting it apart from tours using regular air services.

Finally, the [33-day luxury journey through South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) covers Peru, Bolivia, and Chile, with Easter Island forming its own block of archaeological excursions. It is designed for an extensive continental journey; such a long route is not necessary if your sole goal is to study Rapa Nui in depth.

## How to compare Easter Island itineraries

| Format | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Island, 3 days](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) | Rapa Nui only |
| [Santiago + island, 6 days](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) | A short combination |
| [Chile + island, 10 days](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) | More days on the island |
| [Chile + Atacama, 12 days](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) | Wider geography |
| [Chile + Argentina, 17 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) | A private grand tour |

For specific accommodation arrangements, guiding languages, prices, and included flights, read the full program of the tour you choose. These details vary across our journeys; each has its own terms. Some tours feature Rapa Nui as a main stage, while others offer it as an extension to a busy mainland journey.

## What to check when planning your trip

First decide how many days you want to spend exploring Rapa Nui's archaeology. If Rano Raraku, Tongariki, Orongo, and Anakena are the main goal, start with the island's shorter programs. If the Atacama Desert or Patagonian glaciers also appeal to you, compare the wider routes and the number of flights involved.

Next comes island logistics. An ocean separates Rapa Nui from mainland Chile, and visits to protected archaeological sites must follow the national park's current rules. Flights, arrival times, permitted visiting areas, and guiding arrangements all need to be coordinated. This matters especially on tightly scheduled three-day itineraries.

Also explore [all tours in Chile](/chile/tour/) and [the country's cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) to compare Rapa Nui with other destinations. If the island remains your priority, choose based on actual island days rather than the longest overall tour duration.

## Frequently asked questions about Easter Island tours

### How many days does it take to see the main moai sites?

The published [three-day itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki, Rano Kau, Orongo, Ahu Akivi, and other sites. It is a compact program with excursions every day. A longer stay makes sense if you want free time or a different selection of sites.

### Are Anakena and Orongo included?

Yes. Both feature in several active itineraries, including the [3-day](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), [6-day](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/), and [10-day](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) tours. The precise order and conditions depend on your chosen trip.

### Can I combine Easter Island with Patagonia?

Yes. Such combinations are available in the [12-day Chile and Argentina itinerary](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/) and the [17-day private grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/). Additional travel between different parts of the continent is required.

## El Peral: climbing from the port city to Cerro Alegre

Valparaíso is best explored on two levels: down by the port and up on the hills. El Peral links these parts of the city. Its lower station stands near [Plaza Sotomayor](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/), while the upper station opens onto [Paseo Yugoslavo](/chile/place/paseo-yugoslavo/).

## What to combine with a visit

We include the funicular on our [Viña del Mar and Valparaíso excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/). Along the coast, you visit the [Quinta Vergara Amphitheater](/chile/place/quinta-vergara-amphitheater/), Avenida San Martín, and Avenida Perú; in the port city, you see Plaza Sotomayor, El Peral, and Paseo Yugoslavo.

On our [15-day journey through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), this outing takes place on day ten. You depart from Santiago and return there for the night. Exploring Valparaíso's hills therefore becomes part of a longer itinerary rather than a separate journey with your luggage.

## What to know before the ascent

El Peral is a rail funicular with a small cabin. If riding the funicular itself is essential to your visit, we will check whether it is operating on the excursion date before you book. A stop at the landmark is not an unconditional guarantee that the transport mechanism will be running.

The route continues on foot after the upper station, so comfortable shoes are useful both for steps and for the promenade. If you have mobility restrictions, we can discuss the relevant sections in advance: the short ride does not make the entire hilly route accessible without stairs.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this an aerial cable car with suspended cabins?

No. El Peral's car travels on inclined rails between two levels of the city.

### Where does the upper station lead?

To Paseo Yugoslavo on Cerro Alegre, near Baburizza Palace.

### Is the palace museum included in the same itinerary?

The sightseeing excursion lists El Peral and Paseo Yugoslavo. A separate visit inside the museum galleries can be arranged additionally.

## A journey via El Peral Funicular: how the itinerary works

To experience this landmark as part of a longer journey, we offer a [15-day tour of Brazil, Argentina, Chile, and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). The program connects Rio de Janeiro, both sides of Iguazú Falls, Buenos Aires, Santiago, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Cusco, and Lima.

## When you visit the landmark

In the Chilean section, we first explore Santiago before heading to the coast. [El Peral Funicular](/chile/place/el-peral-funicular/) is included in the group [excursion to Viña del Mar and Valparaíso](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/) on day ten. Afterwards, we return to Santiago for the night; the following day is reserved for the flight to Peru.

## What to consider when booking

We check whether the funicular is operating on the date of your visit. A stop at El Peral does not include a separate tour of the museum galleries near its upper station.

The price of the 15-day tour includes accommodation with breakfast, transfers and excursions specified in the program, entrance tickets, and the Vistadome train to Machu Picchu. International and domestic flights are paid for separately. The price depends on the accommodation selected; the current options and terms are detailed in the complete tour itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to book the excursion separately?

The excursion is already part of the stated 15-day tour. If you only want this section of the journey, we can discuss booking the [standalone excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/).

### Can I add more stops?

We will discuss your preferences before booking and confirm the itinerary. Museums, concerts, and special services not listed in the program are not automatically included.

## El Tatio geysers: how to see the geothermal field at sunrise

**El Tatio is a high-altitude geothermal field in the Chilean Andes, at more than 4,300 m above sea level.** Steam escapes through openings in the ground, hot water bubbles in natural pools, and in the morning the white plumes are particularly striking against the cold air and volcanic slopes. It is among the most unusual natural sites visited from [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

What makes El Tatio distinctive is the combination of **a very early departure, low temperatures, and high altitude**. The visit feels very different from trips to [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) or [Death Valley](/chile/place/death-valley-atacama/), although all three attractions are in northern Chile.

## Why the steam is more visible at sunrise

Water heated deep underground rises to the surface through cracks. Across the geothermal field you can see fumaroles, small eruptions of water, and boiling pools. **Not every plume of steam is an erupting geyser:** the field contains several forms of geothermal activity.

In the morning, when the air is particularly cold, water vapor condenses and becomes easier to see. The plumes consequently look denser and stand out more clearly against the dawn sky. This is the main reason excursions depart well before sunrise.

The intensity of individual eruptions and their visibility depend on natural processes and weather. Neither the height of a particular jet nor the timing of the next eruption can be guaranteed. The purpose of the trip is to experience the geothermal field as a whole, follow the permitted route safely, and observe different kinds of activity.

## Where are the geysers and how long is the drive?

According to the official Chile Travel portal, El Tatio lies about **80 km from San Pedro de Atacama**. The road crosses high-altitude terrain, including stretches of gravel. The drive takes approximately **1.5 hours**, although road conditions, weather, and transport affect the actual duration.

Departures are generally planned for around 4–5 a.m. so visitors can reach the field by sunrise. The actual departure time depends on the season and the confirmed excursion. It helps to plan for the early start the previous evening: if the day ends with a late outing or stargazing session, the morning can feel particularly demanding.

Along the way there are wide-open highland landscapes. Near wetland areas of the Altiplano, you may sometimes spot vicuñas and birds. These are possible wildlife sightings, not guaranteed encounters with any particular species. Some itineraries stop in [Machuca](/chile/place/machuca/) on the return journey.

## Altitude, freezing temperatures, and safety

Above 4,300 m the air is thinner and exertion feels more difficult than in San Pedro. Headaches, weakness, and other signs of poor altitude tolerance can occur. Scheduling the excursion immediately after a flight, without time to acclimatize, is particularly unwise for anyone sensitive to altitude. If serious symptoms develop, inform the accompanying staff and stop ascending. People with medical conditions affected by low oxygen levels should seek medical advice in advance.

**Dawn temperatures can be bitterly cold, even when the desert is warm during the day.** Chile Travel warns of temperatures below freezing and the possibility of severe frost. Bring a warm jacket, hat, gloves, and several layers of clothing. Water, sunglasses, and skin protection are useful for the return journey as well: the high-altitude sun is intense.

The most serious hazards on the field itself are hot water and thin, sometimes unstable ground. Stay on marked paths only. Never approach the edge of a boiling pool for a photograph, test the water with your hand, or step beyond barriers. Age restrictions and other admission conditions should be checked with the geothermal site's administration before traveling.

## How to choose an El Tatio excursion

We offer several standalone excursions with a shared aim—seeing the geysers at sunrise—but with different confirmed activities and inclusions.

- [El Tatio and Machuca: Geysers at Sunrise](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/). A half-day group trip with breakfast, also featuring a thermal pool and a stop in Machuca. Entrance to the geyser field is included.
- [El Tatio: Sunrise Geysers and Thermal Pool](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-dawn-breakfast-thermal-pool/). An itinerary with breakfast, a visit to a natural pool, and a return to San Pedro.
- [El Tatio at Sunrise with Outdoor Breakfast](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-geysers-dawn-outdoor-breakfast/). Focuses on an early visit to the field and breakfast amid the Andean landscape.

A thermal pool mentioned in a particular itinerary does not automatically mean swimming will be possible on every date: access depends on the site's current operating conditions. Compare the stops, included tickets, duration, and participant restrictions, rather than choosing by title alone.

## How to include the geysers in a tour of Chile

On the [Chile: An Otherworldly Journey tour](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/), El Tatio follows days spent exploring San Pedro and other natural sites in Atacama. This is a sensible sequence: lower valleys first, then an early excursion to the highlands.

The [Hidden Treasures of Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes the geysers on a longer journey through other parts of the country. If Atacama is your main priority, look beyond the overall tour duration and check how much time is actually allocated to high-altitude excursions and rest between them.

It helps to distinguish visits by their physical demands:

| Place | What to consider |
|---|---|
| [Death Valley](/chile/place/death-valley-atacama/) | Lower desert valleys, sun, and sand |
| [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) | Walks and sunset stops |
| El Tatio | Above 4,300 m, freezing cold, departure at night |

This order can help distribute the exertion, but it does not guarantee good altitude tolerance. A journey continuing to the Bolivian Altiplano involves even more high-altitude sections; the sequence and time allowed for acclimatization should be agreed in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about the El Tatio geysers

### Why do excursions to the geysers depart at night?

To arrive for sunrise, when cold air makes the steam plumes most visible. The drive from San Pedro takes approximately 1.5 hours, so departures are often around 4–5 a.m.

### How high is El Tatio?

The geothermal field is more than **4,300 m above sea level**. The difference from the town of San Pedro is substantial, so altitude and how you feel need to be considered separately from temperature.

### Can I walk right up to a boiling geyser?

No. Visitors should stay on marked routes and respect barriers. Hot water, steam, and unstable ground can cause severe burns.

### Is breakfast included in the excursion?

Breakfast is included in several standalone [Ada Tours excursions to El Tatio](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/). Check the full list of inclusions for your chosen option, as the programs differ.
